Polyphemus. A Cyclops giant with a single massive eye in the center of his forehead, famous for his encounter with Odysseus in Homer's epic. He was born from Poseidon and the sea nymph Thoosa, one of the one-eyed giants. Despite his strength and size, Polyphemus was remarkably simple-minded, a shepherd who kept flocks of enormous sheep in a cave on the island of Sicily.

His eye, the size of a wagon wheel, was positioned in the center of his forehead and could see considerable distances. Trapped in the monster's cave with several of his men, Odysseus outsmarted the brutish giant through deception. He told Polyphemus that his name was Nobody, so when the Cyclops cried out that Nobody is killing me, the other Cyclopes thought he was mad and came to no one's aid. After blinding the giant's eye with a heated stake, Odysseus escaped by clinging to the undersides of sheep as they left the cave. After his blinding, Polyphemus called upon his father Poseidon to curse Odysseus, resulting in years of divine punishment and wandering. His parentage made him partially divine, giving him immortality despite his lost eye.
